saints.name: Xenia of Saint Petersburg
saints.dates: Eighteenth century; precise dates not established here

summary.text: Xenia is remembered as a widow and Fool-for-Christ in Saint Petersburg. The OCA life explicitly notes the limited information about her early life and family. It describes her bereavement, renunciation of possessions, and life among the city's people, followed by veneration at her grave. The profile preserves those documentary limits rather than supplying precise unsupported birth and death dates.

blocks.text: Xenia lived in eighteenth-century Saint Petersburg. She was married to an army officer named Andrew and was widowed at twenty-six.

blocks.text: She adopted her husband’s name and military clothing and lived without a settled home. The church account describes this as foolishness for Christ: she endured ridicule, accepted little for herself, helped poor people, and secretly carried bricks for a church being built in the Smolensk cemetery. Accounts of prophecy and healing belong to the devotional tradition surrounding her.

blocks.text: The Greek Archdiocese’s reading preserves a period of eight years during which Xenia was absent from Saint Petersburg. It presents a stay in a hermitage as a belief about that interval, rather than an established itinerary. The same reading places her return in her husband’s military clothing before describing her wandering life and prayer for him.
